guidance.title: Patch 1.17.2 decision playbook
guidance.summary: One-time Patch 1.17.2 strategy review for Gold+ play, 17 October 2026. Tier grades, hero counterplay, counter picks, build adaptations, compositions and working pools were re-checked against the 1.17.2 ability text, the official 1.17.2 changes and the 1.17.2 build plans. The 1.17.2 results cover about four days; 16 grades moved, each on a 1.17.2 kit change with evidence pointing the same way, or on a sample whose interval excludes the 1.17 reference. The playbook still favors a coherent win condition over assembling five high win rates.
notes: Jungle: Khaimera (sustained pressure) and Aurora (layered magical control) are the S starting points on 1.17.2. Khaimera rose to S: 1.17.2 raised Ambush's bonus physical scaling and gave it a flat 40% slow, and he is the most-played Gold+ jungler at 55.7% over 2,501 games. Zarus moved to A: 1.17.2 cut Coliseum's damage and his base physical power, and his results fell below his 1.17 reference; he remains the containment pick for a mid or support to convert. Serath (A) is the second-wave diver. Steel is the direct tank catch, with a small jungle sample and Heavy Metal attacks that do not break spell shields. Rampage stays A as a durable long-range boulder catch. Sevarog rose to A on faster Siphon clears, a longer Colossal Blow and a passive-stack fix, and Bayle rose to B on his buffs. Jungle camps now first spawn at 0:20 instead of 0:05 and the river buff at 0:30, so plan the first clear and any early invade around the later start.

Mid: The Fey (prepared area control) is the S starting point. 1.17.2 trimmed Harvest Nettles and Bramble Patch, but her results stayed inside her interval and above the role average, so S is retained and flagged for recheck. Lt. Belica moved to A: 1.17.2 lowered Seismic Assault and Void Bomb damage, lengthened Seismic Assault's cooldown and cut Innovation's haste, and her results fell below her 1.17 reference; she is still the compact catch. Renna rose to A on a stronger Mortal Coil (more damage and scaling, an 8% execute threshold) and a passive-stacking fix. Gideon, Argus, Gadget and Howitzer are A alternatives; a Ground effect such as Valmont's bind stops Torn Space, so protect Gideon's entry and channel. Morigesh stays B. Valmont stays B after 1.17.2 trims to Rupture, Exsanguinate and Lilith. Neon fell to C: no kit change, but 46.7% over 901 games falls below his 1.17 reference.

Carry: Drongo, Sparrow and Eden stay S. Drongo supplies silence and physical shred; 1.17.2 trimmed his base power, health and armor, but his results stayed inside the interval, so S is retained and flagged for recheck. Sparrow needs protected attack time, and Eden rewards practiced heat and stance management. Legion (A) adds area pressure through his Scorched Earth plan. Kira and TwinBlast are the A alternatives; TwinBlast rose on Vaporize and Vortex Grenade buffs, a move that rests on the buffs because his rise sits inside the interval. Revenant fell to B after 1.17.2 trims to Bounty Hunter, Obliterate, Reckoning and his health. Murdock rose to B on more base power, health regeneration and attack speed growth.

Support: choose Mourn for catch plus sustain, Muriel for amplification and protection when initiation already exists, Narbash for a grouped fight, or Steel for a direct opening. Mourn, Muriel and Narbash stay S; position Muriel carefully, since 1.17 left Reversal weaker and costlier. Steel moved to A without a kit change: 49.4% over 2,381 Gold+ games falls below his 51.5% 1.17 reference. Phase and Lt. Belica stay A. The Fey support fell to B after the Harvest Nettles and Bramble Patch trims, on a small sample. Riktor remains a B hook-execution option and Dekker stays B; both rose without a kit change, and a higher rate alone never raises a grade.

Offlane: no offlaner holds S on 1.17.2. Greystone leads the working pool as a lane-pressure option at 51.0% over 2,052 games; 1.17.2 trimmed Assault The Gates' refund on a hero hit, and Stone Forged Soul is a 2.5s stasis heal, not an extra life. Shinbi supplies magical skirmishing after a small All-Kill trim. Kwang rose to A: 1.17.2 lengthened his tether to 1.45s and raised Surge and Fury damage and his cleave. Grux fell to B on lower base power and a costlier Double Pain; he still punishes reachable melee fights, though a Ground effect interrupts Stampede. Akeron (B) supplies sustain and frontline on a health build. Scarlett and Iggy & Scorch are A alternatives, Iggy only when another role supplies frontline. Countess fell to B without a kit change as her results dropped. Terra rose to B on a stronger Highland Hurl. Serath offlane stays C and does not inherit another role's grade.

Pred.gg 1.17.2 matchup rows cover about four days and pool all roles, and the counter, anti-counter and lane-counter views are one table, not separate evidence. They describe observed games with the named hero present, not proof of a lane or ability interaction. Use the reviewed counterplay to decide which response you can execute.

Community builds are alternative hypotheses. The build reviews compared their item sequences with current item effects and your role plan, and the 1.17.2 build pass of 17 October changed no plan part on win rate alone; popularity or a high conditional build rate cannot establish that a purchase caused the wins.

Patch 1.17.2 strategy review (17 October 2026) is a one-time pass, not a recurring schedule. Tier grades, hero notes, counters, build adaptations, compositions and pools were re-checked against the 1.17.2 ability text, the official 1.17.2 notes, the 1.17.2 build pass (90 active plans, 7 experimental unresolved) and the Pred.gg Gold+ 1.17.2 sample. A grade moved with a 1.17.2 kit reason and evidence pointing the same way, or one step under the drop rule when an interval over 500 or more games excluded the 1.17 reference: Khaimera jungle A to S; Zarus jungle, Lt. Belica midlane and Steel support S to A; Sevarog jungle, Renna midlane, Kwang offlane and TwinBlast carry B to A; Countess offlane, Grux offlane, Revenant carry and The Fey support A to B; Bayle jungle, Terra offlane and Murdock carry C to B; Neon midlane B to C. The other 70 grades were retained. The 24 September 1.17 review and its rechecks remain background.

compositions.name: Containment into Black Hole
compositions.plan: Zarus identifies the reachable target before Coliseum; Gideon follows only after key interrupts are covered. Push the nearby wave before moving together to the objective entrance. Protect Gideon through the first 2.75s; then he can reposition while Black Hole finishes. A short catch does not guarantee the full channel.
compositions.weakness: The arena is not a stun, and 1.17.2 lowered Coliseum's damage, so Black Hole, not the leap, has to deliver the kill. Escapes and a broken channel shield can defeat the follow-up, and since 1.17 a Ground effect such as Valmont's bind stops Torn Space, so plan Gideon's entry around it or have Zarus break the bind with control first.

compositions.name: Direct catch, compact burst
compositions.plan: Steel confirms Shield Bash or Shield Slam; Belica follows with Seismic Assault and Void Bomb without wasting both controls at once. Convert the pick into nearby vision or an objective.
compositions.weakness: Two control tools do not replace damage economy, and 1.17.2 lowered Belica's Seismic Assault and Void Bomb damage and lengthened Seismic Assault's cooldown, so a wasted stun costs more. Steel's 1.17.2 jungle sample is still small, and since 1.17 his Heavy Metal attacks do not break spell shields, so bring another answer before the stun.

compositions.name: Second-wave dive
compositions.plan: Mourn creates the first catch while Serath waits for enemy peel, then enters the reachable target. Keep a response beside the allied carry instead of both chasing the reset.
compositions.weakness: No takedown means no visage extension. An early unsupported Serath entry defeats the plan.

compositions.name: Buy time for Sparrow
compositions.plan: Muriel times amplification and protection to a safe firing window; Sparrow attacks the nearest useful target. Other roles must provide the opening and a durable body.
compositions.weakness: This duo lacks dependable long-range initiation; it cannot solve a flank by damage alone.

compositions.name: Protect the channel
compositions.plan: Set the target with Zarus, reserve protection for Gideon’s entry and channel, and keep Reversal for a valid distant commitment. Leave a route back toward the carry. Protect Gideon through the first 2.75s; then he can reposition while Black Hole finishes. A short catch does not guarantee the full channel.
compositions.weakness: Spending all protection on the first entry exposes the next fight. Do not assume a shield survives burst or anti-shield: 1.17 lowered Reversal's damage reduction and raised its cost, and a Ground effect now stops Torn Space, so Muriel's protection cannot guarantee Gideon's entry.

compositions.name: Catch, silence, convert
compositions.plan: Layer a confirmed stun into Belica’s burst; Drongo uses silence to obstruct the response and keeps attacking within Rad Rounds. Plan the airborne blast direction before using it.
compositions.weakness: No sustain support is included yet. Reserve another role for protection and avoid displacing the focus out of allied damage.

compositions.name: Grouped sustain and cleanup
compositions.plan: Aurora controls the approach, Narbash follows with Thunk and grouped sustain, and Legion places physical area pressure on the held route. Move together before starting the objective; since a 1.17.2 fix, allies on Aurora's Glacial Charge ice gain its movement speed.
compositions.weakness: The control is partly delayed. Anti-heal, dispersed targets or a second flank can break the grouped fight.

compositions.name: Peel before damage
compositions.plan: Steel takes the first contact while retaining a control tool for the diver. Muriel keeps Sparrow firing; only commit the objective when the remaining roles can provide magical damage and wave control.
compositions.weakness: The trio alone has no dedicated magical damage plan and can overcommit its only initiating tank.

compositions.name: Controlled front-to-back
compositions.plan: Greystone pressures space while Steel or Mourn confirms the catch. Gideon follows; Sparrow attacks from behind the second body. Keep one support control for the counter-dive and use the won space for objectives. Protect Gideon through the first 2.75s; then he can reposition while Black Hole finishes. A short catch does not guarantee the full channel.
compositions.weakness: Do not overlap every control or throw all three frontliners into the channel area. Greystone's Stone Forged Soul is a 2.5s stasis heal that slows nearby enemies, not an extra life and not peel for Sparrow; 1.17 lowered his base health and armor growth, and 1.17.2 trimmed Assault The Gates' cooldown refund on a hero hit from 35% to 30%, so he re-enters a little less often.

compositions.name: Compact catch with protection
compositions.plan: Use Zarus or Belica to identify a single target, Drongo to constrain the response, and Muriel to protect the actual damage window. Akeron occupies the close entrance while the team keeps a ranged exit.
compositions.weakness: Akeron and Zarus can overcommit together. Disengage from failed catches rather than chase past Muriel and the carries.

compositions.name: Prepared objective control
compositions.plan: Arrive first, establish vision and layer Aurora/Fey control over Legion’s physical area damage; since a 1.17.2 fix, Aurora's Glacial Charge ice speeds allies who walk on it. Narbash supports the grouped advance while Greystone occupies the second angle.
compositions.weakness: Several effects require time and enemies remaining nearby. Do not force into spread ranged poke or ignore a flank while standing together.

compositions.name: Protected second entry
compositions.plan: Akeron and Steel establish contact; Belica confirms a target. Serath waits for peel to be spent while Eden maintains a reachable firing pattern. Save one Steel control for the counter-dive.
compositions.weakness: Two mechanical damage picks make execution demanding. Do not send both into the first control rotation or assume a reset will repair a failed opening.

build_advice.name: Protect the first decisive channel
build_advice.text: Gideon's midlane plan buys Truesilver Bracelet as its protected-channel default, trading early flat penetration for survival of the Black Hole channel; Narbash opens with it to protect the start of Crash Bang Boom!. The bracelet grants control immunity only while its shield holds, and damage or anti-shield can remove that protection. Against little interrupt pressure, Gideon can buy Wraith Leggings earlier.

build_advice.name: Separate clear from catch utility
build_advice.text: Dynamo pays off only when you immobilize an enemy and allies hit it during the next 2.5s. The Riktor, Steel and Terra jungle plans pair Fire Blossom's burn clear with Dynamo for the catch; Overlord is the farming and health-stacking opener for plans where you are not the sole initiator, such as Greystone, Khaimera and Rampage, and since a 1.17.2 fix stacking items such as Overlord also gain stacks passively. Do not buy both clear openers by habit while the next objective needs armor and catch utility.

build_advice.name: Serath: finishing chain versus a marked duel
build_advice.text: Weald is the default Eternal for Serath's attack-speed and on-hit jungle plan. The 2.32 build review switched it from Thraex to Weald because Weald led in the 1.16 loadout samples; those are separate conditional samples, not a causal test, and the Gold+ 1.17.2 loadout samples do not separate the choice from its alternatives by more than chance. Dryad's Boon still shortens basic-ability cooldowns on each attack, and Wind-Rider, which follows her teleport or leap entry, gives less attack speed since 1.17. Weald fires only against a hero below 30% health, with a 10s cooldown per hero, and 1.17.2 lowered its missile damage and on-hit modifier (30% to 20%), so it does not amplify every attack. Keep Thraex for a deliberately sustained marked-target duel.

build_advice.name: Carry buffs must fit the firing pattern
build_advice.text: Marshal fits repeated basic attacks. Revenant’s burst and Legion’s attack-speed conversion require their own item interpretation; do not buy a generic support aura simply because the ally occupies Carry.

guidance.historical_note: One-time review for patch 1.17.2, written on 17 October 2026 as a Gold+ (ranks 27-36) reference. Grades are dated editorial judgments, not win probabilities. Evidence limits: Pred.gg 1.17.2 Gold+ data (version 169, collected 17 October 13:19 CDT) cover about four days since the 13 October release, roughly 9,000 games per role and from 78 to about 2,700 games per hero and role, with intervals of roughly 2 to 11 points either way; Bronze+ figures contain the Gold+ games and are not independent; the 1.17 reference samples are from the previous patch line. The 24 September 1.17 review and its rechecks remain background, and observed rates, calculated kit fit and personal working pools stay separate.

builds.why: Trade behind Iron Rose, then use Imperial Lash or Queen’s Garden to create the damage window. Tyrant of Thorns makes this a durable close-range pressure plan; Royal Flourish supplies damage and movement, not mesmerize. Keep the wave in a position that your jungler can reach.
builds.caution: Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish's control, so the root must come from Imperial Lash or Queen's Garden. Fist Of Razuul's empowered attack needs its combat stacks first. Burn damage pushes the wave; do not let passive clear drag you past safe vision.

builds.review_scope: 1.17.2 patch-targeted build review (17 Oct 2026): supporting mechanics, official 1.17.2 changes and Pred.gg 1.17.2 Gold+ item, crest and loadout samples, checked against the 1.17 plan. Tier, composition and strategy guidance were not reviewed and keep their 1.17 dates.

item_notes.reason: Health supports her health-scaled damage. After the item builds its combat stacks, land the empowered basic attack for its damage and heal instead of treating it as a spell proc.
Each cast empowers the next attack with health-scaling area magic damage and a slow, so weave an attack between Royal Flourish and Imperial Lash. Health and armour support the close-range trade.
Melee hits stack ability damage twice as fast, so a sustained trade raises Crown of Thorns and Royal Flourish damage. The stacks fall off 3 seconds after contact ends.
Burn supplies nearby wave pressure while Royal Flourish is cycling. Health also supports her true-damage scaling; this is not permission to ignore the lane’s damage type.
Health and magical armor support Iron Rose’s defensive job. The extra armor requires being immobilized; it is not permanently active.
Heavy physical defense is for sustained attack pressure. Iron Rose uses both armor types; replace this late physical slot when magical threats are the actual problem.

abilities.RMB:
Adele unfurls her Sword in a straight line, dealing 40/55/70/85/100 (+80% physical power) true damage to all Enemies it passes through.
If she hits an Enemy Hero or Monster, they are Rooted for 0.6s and Adele dashes to the furthest target hit.
abilities.Q:
Adele swings her sword, gaining 40% Movement Speed for the duration.. She deals 5/20/35/50/65 (+50/60/70/80/90% physical power) physical damage twice to nearby Enemies and Mesmerizes them for 1s. Mesmerized Enemies are immune to Slows.
Adele then slams her sword down in an area to deal 60/80/100/120/140 (+8% health) true damage to all Enemies hit.
abilities.E:
Adele equips her shield for 4.5s, increasing her hitbox size and gaining 20/22.5/25/27.5/30% (+4% physical armor)(+4% magical armor) Damage Reduction. This can be cast during other abilities.
On cast, she attaches a Thorned Vine to Enemy Heroes and Monsters within 800u. The Vine deals 6/8/10/12/14 (+0.7% health) true damage every 0.5s for the duration. The Vine snaps if an Enemy moves more than 1000u away.
abilities.R:
Adele performs a small leap, slamming her shield into the ground, summoning a large Thornbush at her location for 8s. 
Vines attach to all Enemies within the central section, dealing 55/90/125 (+5% health) physical damage. This Interrupts abilities, Roots Enemies for 0.5s, and pulls flying Enemies to the ground.
All Enemies inside the Thornbush are Slowed by 35/37.5/40% and take 4/7/10 true damage every 35u moved within it.
abilities.Passive:
Damaging Enemy Heroes applies Thorns to the target for 4s. Additional applications refresh the duration. Cannot be applied to Epic Monsters.
Allies deal 5% of their damage as bonus true damage to Enemies afflicted by Thorns.

builds.why: Imperial Lash and Royal Flourish create the opening, and Seeds of Dominion leaves a thornbush under the Lash target that slows and returns the dash sooner. Dawnstar weakens the heroes you attack and Xenia shields an ally standing next to you, so lane presence becomes protection. Your kit deals physical and true damage; a caster anti-heal item is a poor default.
builds.caution: A long Lash can separate you from the carry, and Xenia only shields allies within 200 units. Dawnstar's attack-speed bonus needs an immobilize first. Tainted Charm needs sustained proximity; replace the anti-heal flex item when healing is not a problem.

Both armours, and standing within 200 units of an ally shields them once per cooldown, which suits a support who stays beside the carry.
Lash and Flourish can immobilize, opening Dynamo’s brief damage-amplification window.
Longer engagements can justify recovery and health after the affordable team tools. Move an actual matchup defense ahead of it.
Protect nearby allies with both armors while holding the front. Its aura does not follow an ally outside range.
Apply anti-heal by remaining near the affected enemy, independent of magical damage. This is a flex answer, not assumed enemy healing.

abilities.RMB:
Akeron deals 70/90/110/130/150 (+65% physical power)(+35% magical power)(+4.5% health) physical damage in a cone. Enemies close to Akeron take 1.35x damage.

abilities.Q:

Each fireball deals 18/29/40/51/62 (+14% magical power) magical damage and Slows Enemies by 7%, up to a max of 35%. 
If an Enemy is within range, the Eye will fire an additional homing fireball at them. Each subsequent hit on the same Target deals 20% less damage, stacking up to a 80% reduction.

abilities.E:
Akeron fires a web, stopping on the first Target hit and causing various effects depending on the Target's type.

World: Lashes to it for up to 5s. While attached to terrain, Akeron can use abilities or leap to the ground, dealing 60/85/110/135/160 (+50% physical power)(+30% magical power) physical damage, Knocking Up, and Stunning Enemies for 1s.

abilities.R:
Akeron Slows himself by 35% while Pulling and dealing 15/20/25 (+4% magical power) magical damage to all Enemies in a cone every 0.25s for 3s.

abilities.Passive:
Akeron gains up to 100 stacks of Hunger, each granting 0.25% increased healing and lasting 3s and refreshing on application.

builds.title: Maintain the spell stream after the catch
builds.why: Use the orb and crystal to constrain a target, then maintain safe Shredder contact. Azure Core supports the mana demand and Entropy rewards repeated ability damage within its per-target trigger limit. Reposition before committing the beam channel; a jungle catch buys time to land successive beams.
builds.caution: Repeated projectiles do not bypass item cooldowns. The crystal can move both enemies and allies, so its placement matters. Bring Spellbreaker forward when a single interrupt prevents you delivering the channel. Lich now grants 4%/7%/10%/14% magical lifesteal, below the retained source description.

item_notes.reason: Mana and haste support the sustained Shredder cast; stack Azure through farm rather than assuming its completed bonus immediately.
Repeated ability damage fits Entropy’s short per-ability trigger interval and the kit’s stacking pressure; it is not an unlimited proc per projectile.
Power, flat penetration and movement support the low-health beam finish. The extra item damage is conditional on target health.
Magical penetration answers armor on the target you can reach. Buying it does not guarantee repeated beam hits.
A single-block shield protects an important cast window and adds magical defense; the extra power depends on the shield remaining active.
Late raw power follows mana, penetration and the first defense. Delay this slot if the enemy can still stop your channel.

builds.why: Track a target through the scent trail, dash for contact and keep attacking through the canister window. Weald's missiles apply on-hit effects to low-health heroes and Dryad's Boon shortens your cooldowns with every attack, so sustained contact matters more than the first hit. previous_review.title: Turn the canister window into a sustained chase
previous_review.why: Track a target through the scent trail, dash for contact and keep attacking through the canister window. Weald's missiles apply on-hit effects to low-health heroes and Dryad's Boon shortens your cooldowns with every attack, so sustained contact matters more than the first hit. item_notes.reason: Spirit Of Amir opens with power, health, haste and an explicit monster-damage effect. Its lifesteal applies in jungle terrain; the power bonus applies outside. These are location-dependent benefits, not two simultaneous buffs or a measured clear-time estimate.
Magical lifesteal complements spell damage while the native spin heals. The missing-health bonus is a risk tradeoff, not a reason to stay low on purpose.
Extra health supports close spell cycles and becomes magical power. Its fight stacks require magical damage to heroes.
Use percentage penetration when magical armor starts reducing the combo. No armor target is assumed from hero class alone.
Late power raises the spell package after access and survival are solved. Delay this expensive slot if you cannot safely reach a marked target.
The spell shield can protect the entry from one ability, not every interrupt. Its extra power lasts only while the shield remains available.

builds.title: Turn mana and allied control into a safe channel
builds.why: Farm the mana and damage opening, then buy Truesilver before the decisive grouped channel fights. Enter after allied control connects, keep Torn Space for positioning, and place Black Hole where the target must remain to contest the objective.
builds.caution: This is the protected-channel default, trading early flat penetration for survival of the channel. The bracelet only grants control immunity while its shield holds; damage or anti-shield can remove that protection. Against little interrupt pressure, buy Wraith Leggings earlier. Black Hole becomes non-cancellable after 2.75s of channeling, when Gideon may act. Protect or interrupt the early phase; after that point, prioritize positioning and leaving the zone. Patch 1.17 lowers Event Horizon to 4% target maximum health, reduces Black Hole damage and prevents Torn Space while Grounded.

Magical penetration helps against armor. It does not multiply the kit’s true control duration or make the channel safe.
Power, flat penetration and movement support reaching and finishing a caught target. The low-health bonus is conditional.
Late magical power supports the full spell package once access and protection are covered. A matchup defense can still take priority.

item_notes.reason: Magical power, health and mana; unit kills and takedowns grant bonus experience and it evolves at base after 500, while each cast restores missing health.
Every ability hit adds magic damage, so turrets and oil repeat it through a long fight. Mana and haste support recasting the nest.

builds.title: Keep Rage alive and cleanse at the right moment
builds.why: Secure farm with the five-hit attack window and preserve Rage between nearby fights where practical. Land the leap after allied setup, stay in contact, and use Invigorate for both its cleanse timing and the current-regeneration heal. This health, power, and sustain plan does not buy attack speed to exceed Unleash’s maximum.
builds.caution: Unleash reduces on-hit effectiveness and already reaches maximum attack speed. Extra attack speed primarily affects attacks outside that window. The leap needs a target and is not a free escape; anti-heal and forced separation can dismantle the trade.

item_notes.reason: Health and splash support farming and close trades. Unleash attacks apply reduced on-hit effectiveness, so the item is not five unrestricted full-strength procs.
Repeated physical hits can stack hero armor reduction during the attack or ultimate sequence. It does not add attack speed beyond Unleash’s cap.
Hero or monster damage stacks healing amplification for regeneration and Invigorate. Physical armor helps survive long enough to use it.
The emergency shield buys a brief chance to cleanse and heal. Do not wait below its threshold if the incoming control needs an earlier Invigorate.
Magical armor and increased healing support a sustained trade against magic threats. Anti-heal still reduces the recovery you receive.
Proximity armor reduction helps the physical follow-through after leap. Move it earlier against physical damage; change it when that threat is absent.

item_notes.reason: Spirit Of Amir opens with power, health, haste and an explicit monster-damage effect. Its lifesteal applies in jungle terrain; the power bonus applies outside. These are location-dependent benefits, not two simultaneous buffs or a measured clear-time estimate.
Weave a basic attack after a cast to add magical on-hit damage alongside the energized attack pattern. The item has its own cooldown.
Stay near the tethered target for magic amplification and magical defense. An ally firing at a different target gains no aura benefit.

Percentage magical penetration answers armor when it appears. It does not benefit the thrown-blade true-damage portion through armor reduction.
Use the immobilization-triggered armors against counter-control after entry. It is a flex defense, not extra tether duration.

item_notes.reason: Ability hits build magical-armor reduction while health and omnivamp support trades. The grounded blade’s true-damage strike is a different case from the held magical strike.
A cast primes an empowered magical basic attack, matching energized sword weaving. Its item cooldown is separate from the passive’s cooldown reduction.
Earlier magical armor protects the trade while nearby magical damage benefits from the aura. It does not amplify the grounded blade’s true damage.
The accumulated health becomes power while the shield and repeated magical hits support a longer fight. Fiend stacks have an interval, not one per simultaneous hit.
Magical penetration supports the magical parts against armor. Move it earlier only when armor is limiting damage; it does not improve a true-damage strike.
Health and magic defense help preserve another shield/cast cycle. Its extra armors require being immobilized rather than being always available.

builds.title: Use penetration and ability cycles around the standard
builds.why: The rifle scales with physical penetration and bonus attack speed converts to haste, so this is not a conventional firing-speed build. Scorched Earth leaves napalm zones where Frag Order and Saturation Charge mines explode and under Orbital Sanction, so place them where enemies must stand. Deploy the standard where allies can remain; the defensive finish protects sustained participation rather than promising a burst-only kill.
builds.caution: Cluster mines deal reduced consecutive damage to one target, and napalm zones last 3 seconds, so do not assume every tick lands. Flat penetration thresholds require actually purchased stats; an item's listed speed does not directly become faster rifle fire. Rallying Roar has had a 20-second cooldown since 1.17 (official notes; the Pred.gg tooltip now shows it too).

builds.patch_context: Larger basic projectiles improve hit consistency. They do not increase listed damage or establish a measured DPS gain; retain the attack-dependent build.

builds.title: Clear with mines, then zone with the orbital
builds.why: Mid Legion is a physical area caster: Saturation Charge and Frag Order clear waves and trade, and Scorched Earth leaves napalm where the mines explode and under Orbital Sanction. Malady, Deathstalker and Spear Of Desolation pass 100 physical power and 30 physical penetration, which lengthen the mine slow and widen Orbital Sanction, and the rifle gains damage per point of penetration; Deathstalker's attack speed becomes haste through the passive. Vesh turns a share of ability damage on heroes into a damage-over-time effect, so trade with mines and grenade, then place the orbital where the enemy must stand.
builds.caution: Consecutive mines on one target deal 25% damage and napalm lasts 3 seconds, so this plan clears and zones better than it bursts one target. Frag Order's missing-health bonus needs 45 haste from purchased items: Malady, Spear Of Desolation, The Perforator and Infernum give 43, reaching 51 at the fifth item only if Ortus's 8 counts as a purchased item; haste converted from attack speed is not counted. Mid has no support to peel: Frag Order's self-launch, Rally Point's knockback and Saturation Charge's slow are your defensive tools, so buy Dread earlier into magical burst.

item_notes.reason: Physical power, penetration and haste. Parting Gift makes a killed unit explode for damage based on its maximum health, which helps mines and grenade finish a wave; Demise is a separate trigger on heroes below 40% health.

Penetration raises the rifle's penetration-scaled damage and basic attacks on heroes shred physical armor. Its attack speed, including Onslaught's bonus equal to your penetration, is converted to haste by the passive, not treated as faster firing.
Penetration, haste and 25 ultimate haste. With Malady and Deathstalker it passes the 30 penetration that widens Orbital Sanction, and damage rises 10% for 6 seconds after casting it.
Ignores 30% of physical armor for mine and grenade damage, and ability damage slows by 10% for 1 second. Its 15 haste moves you toward the 45-haste Frag Order bonus.

Damaging abilities and basic attacks apply Kindling; four stacks ignite the target for maximum-health physical damage that grows against bonus armor. The mana and haste support repeated casts, and with this item, item haste reaches 43 (51 if the crest counts). Whether each mine applies its own stack is not stated.

Physical power and penetration with magical armor; Vital Shield blocks 25% of magical damage from a hero for 3 seconds and returns after 15 seconds without hero damage. It is the answer to the magical mid laner; move it earlier into burst.

previous_review.title: Clear with mines, then zone with the orbital
previous_review.why: Mid Legion is a physical area caster: Saturation Charge and Frag Order clear waves and trade, and Scorched Earth leaves napalm where the mines explode and under Orbital Sanction. Malady, Deathstalker and Spear Of Desolation pass 100 physical power and 30 physical penetration, which lengthen the mine slow and widen Orbital Sanction, and the rifle gains damage per point of penetration; Deathstalker's attack speed becomes haste through the passive. Vesh turns a share of ability damage on heroes into a damage-over-time effect, so trade with mines and grenade, then place the orbital where the enemy must stand.
previous_review.caution: Consecutive mines on one target deal 25% damage and napalm lasts 3 seconds, so this plan clears and zones better than it bursts one target. Frag Order's missing-health bonus needs 45 haste from purchased items: Malady, Spear Of Desolation, The Perforator and Infernum give 43, reaching 51 at the fifth item only if Ortus's 8 counts as a purchased item; haste converted from attack speed is not counted. Mid has no support to peel: Frag Order's self-launch, Rally Point's knockback and Saturation Charge's slow are your defensive tools, so buy Dread earlier into magical burst.

builds.title: Trade from health in lane, then open fights with the boulder
builds.why: Offlane Rampage is a health-scaling lane bruiser: Pounce scales with health, Rumble's passive turns health into physical power, and Krix and every item add health. Elafrost empowers the attack after each cast with health-scaled area magic damage and a slow, and its mana regeneration keeps Rumble and Pounce available in a long lane; Overlord's cleave trades and pushes the wave, and minion kills add permanent health. Tainted Guard answers basic-attacking offlaners. Later, throw the boulder from range for your team (Rock & Awe adds damage with distance) and hold space in Behemoth.
builds.caution: The passive's regeneration doubles only in the jungle, so in lane rely on Regenerative Tissue, Behemoth and the passive's heal when immobilised; back off after a lost trade instead of relying on regeneration. Rock & Awe's bonus needs a long throw, which is easier to dodge; in lane the boulder is mainly a stun for your jungler. Move Void Helm ahead of Tainted Guard against a magical laner. Unlike the jungle plan there is no Predator: camp-leader bonuses do not apply in lane.

builds.title: Prepare the fourth shot before choosing the duel
builds.why: Use the firing cycle and Scar to establish a target before committing the fourth shot. Thraex replaces the health-sacrificing default Eternal: its marked-target trade fits a deliberate duel, while Alpha’s Court is conditional on allied distance. The build preserves power, crit and a defensive finish without assuming snowball stacks.
builds.caution: Obliterate splits among targets unless Scar directs it, and repeated missiles deal reduced damage. Reckoning removes the victim from allied follow-up; use it deliberately. Satariel remains an inspectable aggressive alternative with a substantial health tradeoff. In 1.17 Satariel bonus stats fall to 4%, and Demonic Bargain pays at levels 1 and 10 rather than 1, 7 and 13.

builds.title: Wait for a safe descent, then sustain the reset
builds.why: Attack uptime and on-hit damage power this plan. Follow an ally’s catch, use the selected Crushing Descent augment for a brief Ascend stun, and convert the ultimate window into repeated attacks. builds.caution: Base Ascend does not stun: that control belongs to Crushing Descent. Heaven’s Fury applies reduced on-hit effects and repeat-hit damage. Replace a flexible defense with Tainted Rounds only against an actual healing need; anti-heal is no longer assumed in the default six.
builds.rune_note: Weald with Dryad's Boon and Wind-Rider is this plan's choice: Dryad's Boon shortens cooldowns as you attack, and Wind-Rider needs a dash or leap to trigger. Patch 1.17 lowers Wind-Rider's attack speed to 15% but fixes Weald triggering on proc-type damage. Thraex with Savage Strikes and Ferocity remains a sustained-contact alternative; older conditional sample rates do not choose between them.

builds.caution: Heaven’s Fury applies on-hit effects at reduced effectiveness, and repeated strikes on one target also deal reduced damage. The chosen healing items and Savage Strikes support Draconum; do not assume unselected enemies have the same sustain. Anti-heal is a situational replacement.

item_notes.reason: Attack speed, lifesteal and current-health on-hit pressure fit the attack plan. Chastise and Heaven’s Fury use different on-hit effectiveness values.
Moving and attacking prepare a chain-lightning proc for clear and contact. It requires its momentum threshold rather than triggering on every hit.
Physical defense and increased healing support purchased lifesteal and selected Savage Strikes. This is not evidence of native self-healing in the base kit.
Earlier magical defense and threshold cleanse help survive after Ascend. Its brief augment stun does not prevent a full enemy counterattack.
Physical penetration supports ordinary attacks and physical damage against armor. It does not improve the ultimate’s true-damage burn.
The emergency shield and omnivamp help survive an extended commit. Stop chasing when reaching a reset would require entering untouched enemy control.

Wave burn and health support the scaling lane, but manage last hits so an ability earns Souls. The item does not directly satisfy the passive’s ability-kill requirement.
Physical armour against attackers, and each basic attack they land reduces their healing and bleeds them. It answers attack-based lanes, not spell healing.

builds.title: Build Track stacks before releasing the wolves
builds.why: Start Spirit Of Amir for jungle clear and sustain, then Oathkeeper for attacks between casts and Magnify for repeated hero contact. Use an allied catch to keep the target within the wolf circle, build Track and use All-Kill. The small observed three-item core is supporting context; the choice follows these mechanics rather than its high win rate.
builds.caution: Circle Rhythm shields rather than heals. Keep a dash charge for the exit. This is a damage jungler, not your only frontline. World Breaker can replace late Crown when health matters more than the larger power spike; an earlier spell shield still takes priority against a decisive interrupt.

builds.author: Codex editorial review

item_notes.reason: Spirit Of Amir opens with power, health, haste and an explicit monster-damage effect. Its lifesteal applies in jungle terrain; the power bonus applies outside. These are location-dependent benefits, not two simultaneous buffs or a measured clear-time estimate.
Cast then use an empowered basic attack to align Oathkeeper with the Track/attack pattern. Keep a dash available for repositioning.
After the farming opener and cast-attack proc, repeated wolf damage stacks magical-armor reduction on heroes. Health and omnivamp help sustain contact; this is not a shield-to-heal conversion.
Use percentage penetration when the targets build magical armor; Track stacks still have to be earned before the ultimate.
A spell shield can protect one entry against control and adds magical defense. Its extra power disappears when the shield is removed.
Late power improves the marked-target finish after access and protection are covered. It is the flexible final purchase, not a reason to skip necessary defense.

builds.title: Use the firing mode’s actual conversion rules
builds.why: Build power, crit and attack tools around safe firing access. Hypercharge has a fixed firing rate and converts bonus speed into damage, while its on-hit effects are reduced. Flight can extend attack access after allied setup; it is not permission to hover over the enemy team without peel.
builds.caution: Do not multiply a full on-hit item proc by every Hypercharge instance. The ultimate stops at the first hero and flight does not block control. Satariel lowers maximum health with each takedown stack and loses its stacks on death, so a failed dive costs more. Broken Wings stops items and abilities from changing your movement speed, including slows and speed boosts. Patch 1.17 lowers Satariel's per-stack bonus to 4% and pays Demonic Bargain's second 350 gold at level 10.

item_notes.reason: Both powers, speed and temporary hero-hit crit fit the firing modes. During Hypercharge, speed is converted into damage rather than faster firing.

builds.title: Trade, clear, then convert a catch
builds.why: Trade around Cybernetic Shell and Shield Bash, controlling the wave before leaving for a team catch. Heavy Metal rewards armor investment, and Tainted Guard adds armour that punishes enemies who attack you. Flux Matrix turns landed control into an allied magic damage window. Keep Bull Rush available when the enemy jungler is missing.
builds.caution: The first armor component follows the actual lane damage type. Shield Bash’s monster bonus does not increase hero damage. A Force Shield blocks projectiles, not every enemy ability, and a poorly directed Bull Rush can move a target away from your team. In 1.17, Heavy Metal basic attacks no longer remove spell shields; do not use them as the shield-breaking setup.
builds.rune_note: Regenerative Tissue supports recovery between trades. Cannibalism rewards participation in fights; Predator instead requires camp leader kills and should be a route-specific option rather than the default lane assumption. Both choices are valid Krix slots. No full-loadout win rate is inferred.

item_notes.reason: Health and physical armor support the shielded trade and nearby clear. The source’s monster-damage bonus is not part of the hero matchup.
Physical armour feeds Heavy Metal and the armour-scaling kit, and enemies attacking you lose healing and bleed. It answers attack-based lanes; it is not a spell-healing counter.
Magical defense and a nearby magic aura support the catch and allied follow-up. The target must remain in useful range after the knock-up.
Health and magic armor support Cybernetic Shell and its armor interaction. Its reactive armor trigger requires being immobilized.
Health supports Shell and the item’s own empowered attack adds damage and a heal after combat stacks. It replaces a default late out-of-combat recovery purchase.
Physical defense supports Heavy Metal’s armor-based damage and the frontline job. Against a magical threat, adapt the late armor slot instead of preserving this order blindly.

previous_review.title: Trade, clear, then convert a catch
previous_review.why: Trade around Cybernetic Shell and Shield Bash, controlling the wave before leaving for a team catch. Heavy Metal rewards armor investment, and Tainted Guard adds armour that punishes enemies who attack you. Flux Matrix turns landed control into an allied magic damage window. Keep Bull Rush available when the enemy jungler is missing.
previous_review.caution: The first armor component follows the actual lane damage type. Shield Bash’s monster bonus does not increase hero damage. A Force Shield blocks projectiles, not every enemy ability, and a poorly directed Bull Rush can move a target away from your team. In 1.17, Heavy Metal basic attacks no longer remove spell shields; do not use them as the shield-breaking setup.

item_notes.reason: Physical armor supports the selected Heavy Metal augment while proximity damage helps clear. Monster damage belongs to the verified kit, not an invented clear-time estimate.
Multiple immobilizing abilities can open the brief damage-amplification window. Chain them with allies instead of wasting all control at once.
Nearby magical amplification supports the kit and a mid’s follow-up. Magical armor also contributes to the selected Heavy Metal loadout.
Ultimate activation grants a defensive window; incoming basic attacks help refund non-ultimate cooldowns for a second control cycle.
Magical armor and a counter-control trigger are useful when diving a spell threat. It is not a new healing source.
Physical mitigation and armor suit a late frontline slot and Heavy Metal. Choose a different defense when physical damage is not the danger.

builds.patch_context: Attack speed and base attack time move in opposite directions, so do not call this a simple attack-speed buff. Disc recovers cooldown faster, Terminal damage falls, Infuse improves and ultimate returns sooner. Support protection and offlane damage remain different plans.

builds.title: Stack the on-hit DoT from behind your support
builds.why: Carry Zinx is a ranged on-hit attacker, not a healer: every Refibrillator hit adds physical base damage and a stacking magical damage-over-time effect, Prophecy adds magical on-hit damage, and Terminal Treatment raises on-hit damage as the target's health falls. Spectra and Orion supply attack speed (Orion converts item haste), and Typhoon's stacks add more while you keep attacking. Open with Bad Medicine or Ricochet, attack while the slow or stun holds, and keep Infuse for your support and Neural Regenesis for whoever is about to die.
builds.caution: 1.17 raised attack speed to 115% but lengthened base attack time to 1.5, cut Terminal Treatment to 25% and slowed Typhoon's scaling and dash, so do not read this as an attack-speed buff. The official note gives Terminal Treatment 25% (as additional DoT damage), and the current Pred.gg text puts it on Refibrillator's on-hit damage at up to 25%; the plan relies only on that. Zinx has no dash of her own: Typhoon's Mirage at four stacks is the only one, so stand behind your support and buy Spellbreaker earlier into magical burst.

meta_review.author: Claude, 1.17.2 editorial strategy review
meta_review.scope: General ranked planning for Patch 1.17.2 with composition-specific conditions; Gold+ evidence. One-time review; no claim of a professional-play or all-rank consensus.

tier_definitions.S: Priority starting point for its stated job; still depends on draft and execution.
tier_definitions.A: Strong alternative with a clear role or enabling condition.
tier_definitions.B: Situational or practiced pick; check what the team needs.
tier_definitions.C: Lower default priority in this review; favor comfort or a favorable matchup.

meta_review.method: Authored judgments from 1.17.2 kits (Pred.gg version 169), the official 1.17.2 changes, the 1.17.2 build pass plans and role economy, weighed against Pred.gg Gold+ 1.17.2 role results collected 17 October 2026 (about four days since the 13 October release, roughly 9,000 games per role; Bronze+ contains the same games). Each grade was compared with its previous reference sample (the 1.17 review or the 1.17 line). A grade moved at most one step, and only with a kit or patch reason and evidence pointing the same way, or under the drop rule: one step down without a kit reason when a 95% interval over at least 500 games excludes the previous reference rate. A high rate alone never raises a grade, and a sample under 100 games is not graded on alone; the two roles with fewer than 100 Gold+ 1.17.2 games keep their previous sample. Grades are not calculated win probabilities, source-provided tiers, or proven optimal picks. A 3 percentage-point change from the listed sample with at least 500 current games flags the grade for review; that trigger is not a significance test. Refreshing data does not rewrite this review.

entries.why: Iron Rose lets her trade up close, and Imperial Lash or Queen's Garden opens the damage window; Crown of Thorns helps allies convert contact.
entries.watch: Her 1.17.2 offlane results recovered from the early low over a larger sample but still sit below the role average with no kit change, and a rate alone does not raise a grade. Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish's mesmerize, so the offlane damage plan is not the support peel plan.

entries.why: Imperial Lash and Iron Rose give a protected catch; Crown of Thorns helps allies convert contact.
entries.watch: Her 1.17.2 support results sit near the role average, which supports a situational pick rather than more. Tyrant of Thorns removes Royal Flourish control, so the offlane damage plan is not the support peel plan.

entries.why: Crushing Maw sustains close trades and Web Lash creates access; Consume rewards a team that can keep targets nearby.
entries.watch: B since the 3 Oct recheck: 1.17 cut his magical scaling and his jungle results fell below even. Keep the durable health route; interrupted Consume and repeated disengage still deny the plan.

entries.why: Crushing Maw sustains close trades and Web Lash creates access; Consume rewards a team that can keep targets nearby.
entries.watch: B since the 3 Oct recheck: in results the 1.17 magic-scaling cut outweighed the Crushing Maw health-scaling gain. Keep the durable health build rather than a burst plan; interrupted Consume and repeated disengage deny it.

entries.why: Dread Nova opens a ranged damage window and Particle Shredder can keep pressure on a caught target.
entries.watch: The midlane economy supports his damage engine; reposition before committing the beam channel. His 1.17.2 midlane results sit above the role average with no kit change, which confirms A rather than raising it, and 1.17 trimmed Lich in this plan's Vesh blessings.

entries.why: Dread Nova gives a repeatable ranged catch and Ether Crystal changes where the fight happens; Particle Shredder converts the opening when it is safe to channel.
entries.watch: Support income limits his damage engine, and his 1.17.2 Gold+ support results sit below even and well below his midlane results. Pick him only when the team already has a durable entry.

entries.why: Glacial Charge, its Glacial Thorns root crystals and Hoarfrost give repeatable access, control and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.
entries.watch: Jungle is the priority on current role evidence. Do not transfer that grade to offlane or support, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.

entries.why: Glacial Charge and Hoarfrost give repeatable access and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.
entries.watch: Jungle is the priority on current role evidence. Do not transfer that grade to offlane or support, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.

entries.why: Glacial Charge and Hoarfrost give repeatable access and escape; Cryoseism can punish enemies gathering around an objective.
entries.watch: Her 1.17.2 support results sit near the role average, below her 1.17 rise, and the only 1.17.2 change fixes the ice wall's movement speed, so B holds. Do not transfer the jungle grade, and keep an exit after the first control cycle.

entries.why: Skull Crusher marks and shreds a target and Cursed Edge's third slash stuns, setting up Kingslayer on a reachable catch; Dire Howl returns part of the damage he takes.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 raised Cursed Edge and Skull Crusher scaling, shortened Skull Crusher's cooldown and improved Dire Howl healing, and his jungle results rose to near the role average. He still needs a committed entry; avoid relying on disputed Berserk scaling.

entries.why: Skull Crusher and Cursed Edge can set up a heavy-hit sequence, with Kingslayer converting a reachable catch.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 buffed Skull Crusher, Cursed Edge, Dire Howl and his attack speed growth, but his offlane results stayed well below even, so he remains a comfort pick. Avoid relying on disputed Berserk scaling or assuming faster attacks solve his access problems.

entries.why: Detection Protocol helps locate a route into a fight; Chrono Swipe and Primeval Roar support sustained contact after entry.
entries.watch: Near-even results make this a dependable option rather than a statistical standout. Ursine Burst still needs allied follow-up and an exit plan.

entries.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; the fixed Feast now gives a real targeted conversion after two abilities apply Haemorrhage.
entries.watch: C after the 29 Oct recheck: with no kit change, her 1.17.2 jungle results fell below the role average over a sample more than three times the one first reviewed. Mark a safe Shadow Slip return point before committing Feast, and treat her as a practiced pick only.

entries.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; Feast converts a target after two ability hits apply Haemorrhage.
entries.watch: B on 1.17.2: with no kit change her offlane results fell below even over a sample that excludes her 1.17 rate. Mark a safe Shadow Slip return point and apply Haemorrhage before Feast.

entries.why: Shadow Slip and Blade Siphon support short trades; Feast converts a target after two ability hits apply Haemorrhage.
entries.watch: 1.17 restored Feast's intended damage, but her 1.17.2 midlane results sit below the role average, and midlane still asks a melee hero to trade into ranged lanes. Keep a safe Shadow Slip return and follow the jungler's catch rather than entering first.

entries.why: Re-Crunch rewards correct ability sequencing and Cross Crunch attack weaving; Forward Crunch can preserve access for a second rotation.
entries.watch: The combo breakpoint and sustained contact matter. A Ground effect now interrupts empowered Forward Crunch, so a lost escape can leave him stranded.

entries.why: Re-Crunch rewards correct ability sequencing and Cross Crunch attack weaving; Forward Crunch can preserve access for a second rotation.
entries.watch: The combo breakpoint and sustained contact matter. A Ground effect now interrupts empowered Forward Crunch, and a lost escape can leave him stranded.

entries.why: Control and projectile accuracy can still buy valuable attack time, but the dated Gold+ sample does not support default A priority. Choose for the needed fence and peel tools rather than treating kit fit as demonstrated pair success.
entries.watch: This grade values control despite below-even role results on both patches. Missed skill shots and poor fence timing reduce the benefit substantially.

entries.why: Gag Grenade can deny a response while Rad Rounds supplies a damage window; Shrapnel Cannon adds armor shred and escape utility.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 trimmed his base physical power, health and armor, and his carry results now sit near even, so the S is flagged for recheck. Keep a target in attack range; the airborne blast can displace enemies away from allies.

entries.why: Tachyon Lance/Axiom Strike and Zero Shift let Eden choose a trading pattern; in the Focal Lens plan, a Tachyon Lance hit shreds armor before the physical follow-through.
entries.watch: Heat and stance execution are essential. Her passive turns attack speed into physical power rather than firing speed, and she still needs a response to dive.

entries.why: Safeguard and Hamstring enable short ability-attack trades before Earth Shatter can finish a damaged target.
entries.watch: The dated jungle result was weak and his 1.17.2 jungle results stay below even with no kit change. Ground now stops Reaping Dash's teleport; do not use the finishing ultimate as a substitute for an opening catch.

entries.why: Safeguard and Hamstring enable short ability-attack trades before Earth Shatter can finish a damaged target.
entries.watch: His offlane sample is small in both patches and favors specialists. Reaping Dash can no longer teleport while he is hit by a Ground effect, and the finishing ultimate is not an opening catch.

entries.why: Sticky Mine pressures a position and Tesla Dome punishes enemies held in a choke; Security Gate provides an escape or peel route.
entries.watch: Midlane supplies the farming economy. 1.17.2 made Security Gate reach its range faster and raised Tesla Dome's armor shred, but the gate still costs more mana than before 1.17, so keep it for the exit or a diver.

entries.why: Sticky Mine pressures a position and Tesla Dome punishes enemies held in a choke; Security Gate provides an escape or peel route.
entries.watch: Midlane supplies the farming economy. Support is a smaller-sample damage-utility option when the team already has frontline and reliable initiation.

entries.why: Cosmic Rift supports lane pressure while Torn Space preserves positioning; Black Hole offers a clear conversion for jungle or support control.
entries.watch: 1.17 trimmed Void Breach, Black Hole, Event Horizon and his mana scaling, and Hotfix 1.17.1 removed a Black Hole bug that favored him, so he is an A conversion pick for a coordinated team. A Ground effect now stops Torn Space, and interrupts land once the Truesilver shield breaks.

entries.why: Make Way and Sacred Oath create sustained gank pressure; Stone Forged Soul can extend the time he occupies frontline space.
entries.watch: The offlane result does not transfer to jungle, and 1.17.2 refunds Assault The Gates only on a hero or camp leader hit, so the leap returns less often while clearing. 1.17 lowered his health and armor growth, so buy real defense early; the draft still needs a reliable catch.

entries.why: Make Way and Sacred Oath create sustained lane pressure; Stone Forged Soul can extend the time he occupies frontline space.
entries.watch: 1.17 lowered his base health and armor growth and 1.17.2 trimmed the Assault The Gates refund; his 1.17.2 offlane results sit near even, so he is a strong lane-pressure option rather than the default. Buy real defense on time; personal survival is not allied peel, and the draft still needs a reliable catch.

entries.why: Assault Mode and Pulsefire provide a magical basic-attack threat; Energy Shield can preserve a firing window against an important spell.
entries.watch: His 1.17.2 carry results settled near the role average over a larger sample with no kit change, so treat him as a practiced pick, not a priority. Buy penetration for the magical damage he actually deals, and do not count the shield as a general escape.

entries.why: Smash 'n Grab creates a reachable target and Double Pain rewards continued contact; Warlord's Challenge helps punish a committed melee fight.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 trimmed his base physical power and raised Double Pain's mana cost, and his jungle results sit just under the role average. Long-trade strength does not guarantee access to a ranged target; Ground effects interrupt Stampede, and anti-heal or disengage can stop the plan.

entries.why: Smash 'n Grab creates a reachable target and Double Pain rewards continued contact; Warlord's Challenge helps punish a committed melee fight.
entries.watch: B on 1.17.2: his base physical power fell, Double Pain costs more mana, and his offlane results fell below even over a large sample. A Ground effect interrupts Stampede and long trades do not guarantee access to a ranged target; anti-heal and disengage can stop the plan.

entries.why: R2000 Missile supports ranged pressure and Land Mine can protect an angle; Make It Rain follows a held target with an aimed barrage.
entries.watch: Track the target throughout the ultimate. Movement during the barrage is not immunity, and a poorly aimed mine can spoil allied follow-up.

entries.why: Flame Turret and Oil Spill can control a lane approach and prepare objective space before the fight starts.
entries.watch: The strong offlane result needs composition context: pick ranged lane pressure when another slot supplies frontline. Rotations away from the prepared nest are less comfortable.

entries.why: Flame Turret and Oil Spill can control a lane approach and prepare objective space before the fight starts.
entries.watch: Supply frontline from another slot and set the nest before objectives; rotations away from it are less comfortable. Inferno's turret attack-speed text is a 1.17 description correction, not a new buff.

entries.why: Narcosis can create a catch for Hydroclasm and Brine; Genesis offers a further control and damage window.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 lengthened Narcosis' later cooldowns and cut Genesis damage and slow, and his midlane results stay below even, so he remains a specialist pick. Bubble amplification timing and target access make nominal damage a poor guide to reliable output.

entries.why: Shadow Walk can create an unseen angle and Crippling Dagger helps maintain it before Guillotine finishes a damaged target.
entries.watch: Her jungle results stay below even on 1.17.2 and her kit is unchanged. The fragile entry favors experienced players; vision, enemy peel and the escape route matter more than an attractive burst total.

entries.why: Ambush leaps in and now slows by 40% at every rank, and Unleash keeps the pressure on; Cull converts a caught target and Invigorate extends contact.
entries.watch: S on 1.17.2: Ambush gained physical scaling and a flat slow, and he is the most-played jungler with results above the role average. Lower base armor makes early trades less forgiving, and anti-heal and disengage can still deny sustain beyond allied range.

entries.why: Ambush and Unleash give short trades once Lane Lurker builds Rage from minions; Cull converts a caught target and Invigorate extends contact.
entries.watch: The large jungle result does not transfer: his 1.17.2 offlane results recovered toward even over a larger sample but remain inside the role average's range, with no kit change to lift the grade. Anti-heal and disengage can deny his sustain, especially beyond allied range.

entries.why: Mercy and repeated attacks build Vengeance before Dusk; Shadow Glide offers a way to preserve space or follow a confirmed catch.
entries.watch: 1.17 raised Mercy damage and Dusk refunds mana on a kill, and her 1.17.2 carry results sit near the role average, consistent with A. Purge is an exposed commitment that still needs control or peel, and the refund needs a kill.

entries.why: Judgement of the Heavens can tether a target for sword-centered follow-up; Light of the Heavens and Fury of the Heavens support repeated trades.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 lengthened the tether and raised Surge, Fury and cleave damage, but his jungle results stay just under the role average, so he remains a practiced sword-placement option. Recalling the Blade early breaks the tether, so commit follow-up first.

entries.why: Judgement of the Heavens tethers enemies to the thrown Blade, Surge of the Heavens recalls it with a knock-up, and Fury of the Heavens teleports to the Blade for a slowing strike.
entries.watch: A on 1.17.2: a longer tether and more Surge, Fury and cleave damage came with offlane results above his 1.17 rate and near the role average. Recalling the Blade early breaks the tether, so place it where allies can follow.

entries.why: Saturation Charge and Orbital Sanction offer area pressure alongside ranged attacks; the Scorched Earth plan adds napalm zones where mines, Frag Order and the beam land.
entries.watch: 1.17 widened the rifle projectile, but his 1.17.2 carry results stay near even, below the S carries. The ability-oriented plan converts an allied catch, and bonus attack speed becomes haste, not firing speed.

entries.why: Seismic Assault gives a compact catch into Void Bomb; Neural Disruptor adds a finishing threat that depends on the target's mana state.
entries.watch: A on 1.17.2: Seismic Assault and Void Bomb deal less, Seismic Assault's cooldown is longer and Innovation grants less haste, and her midlane results fell to about even. A missed Seismic Assault line leaves little catch, and maximum-rank Innovation effects still guide skill investment.

entries.why: Seismic Assault gives a compact catch into Void Bomb; Neural Disruptor adds a finishing threat that depends on the target's mana state.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 cut Seismic Assault and Void Bomb damage and lengthened Seismic Assault's cooldown, though her support results sit near the role average. On a support budget Neural Disruptor carries less burst, so the grade rests on landing Seismic Assault for allies.

entries.why: Maco Gift! can sustain an ally around a chosen space, while Maco Strike! supplies control and Maco Fly! changes the supporting angle.
entries.watch: His Gold+ support results stay well below even on 1.17.2 despite useful tools. Healing requires allies to stay in range, and spending Maco Fly! forward can leave him without an exit.

entries.why: A shorter Hive cooldown and Mark set up close-range pressure and healing trades before Curse finishes the marked target.
entries.watch: Still situational: Curse does not solve entering Mark range safely, and rank-one Mark is slower since 1.17. Her 1.17.2 midlane results sit below even with no kit change, so pick her into a reachable target with allied control.

entries.why: Abduct creates a catch while Contagion supplies allied sustain; Beguile offers another response as the fight develops.
entries.watch: Keep a defensive response after initiating. Eclipse connects distant pressure but should not be interpreted as relocating teammates.

entries.why: Static Trap and Buckshot can buy firing space, while Long Arm of the Law converts a distant catch without abandoning the lane.
entries.watch: B on 1.17.2: higher base physical power, health regeneration and attack speed growth came with carry results back near even. Save Buckshot and traps for the diver.

entries.why: Consecrated Ground and Alacrity heal, shield and speed an attacking ally; Reversal Of Fortune can protect a committed teammate across the map.
entries.watch: 1.17 trimmed her durability, passive amplification, Alacrity shield scaling and Reversal's damage reduction, and raised Reversal's cost, yet her 1.17.2 support results remain above the role average. Choose her when the team supplies a way to begin fights.

entries.why: Song Of My People and March! reward a team that moves together; Thunk supplies a catch before Crash Bang Boom! layers pressure.
entries.watch: Grouped sustain, March movement and a direct Thunk catch make him a priority for a team that actually stays in range. Hold the ultimate until interruption can be covered.

entries.why: L.I.N.X and Final Thread offer a deliberate spell sequence, with Data Burst supporting the next empowered tool.
entries.watch: C on 1.17.2: with no kit change her midlane results fell below even over a sample that excludes her 1.17 rate. A practiced pick: correct sequencing and a saved Erase Vector are needed, and true and magical damage use different penetration.

entries.why: Telekinetic Link and Hyperflux can amplify repeated attacks; Energy Lance and a timed pull can buy the linked ally space.
entries.watch: 1.17 lowered her health, Essence Catalyst healing and Hyperflux attack speed, so trades are less safe and amplification is slightly smaller. This stays a partner-dependent grade; a premature pull can undo a good commitment.

entries.why: Boulder Throw creates an accessible catch and King of the Jungle supports the jungle route; Behemoth can extend frontline pressure.
entries.watch: The plan's Rock & Awe rewards long boulder throws, so land the catch from range before committing Pounce. His 1.17.2 jungle results sit just under the role average without a kit change; health does not guarantee uninterrupted target access.

entries.why: Mortal Coil pulls and can execute low targets, Soulfire and Stupor support wave pressure and catch conversion, and Abyssal Rift gives a prepared team a sustained follow-up window.
entries.watch: A on 1.17.2: Mortal Coil gained damage, scaling and a higher execute threshold, a fix restored her passive stacking, and her midlane results rose above the role average. Protect farming and the channel, and avoid collecting Essence through an exposed route.

entries.why: Hellfire Rounds and Obliterate reward a short damage window, making allied catches a natural way to convert his burst.
entries.watch: B on 1.17.2: Bounty Hunter, Obliterate's missiles, Reckoning's cooldown and stat steal and his health were cut, and his carry results fell from his 1.17 rate. Reckoning can remove a focus target from allied area damage; coordinate isolation, and do not buy attack speed merely because it suits another carry.

entries.why: Hook-dependent access and the dated weak Gold+ role result lower default jungle priority. His support catch remains a separate job; a landed hook can still enable excellent follow-up.
entries.watch: The grade depends on landing the hook. Keep an exit and preserve peel after a miss; his support catch is a separate job, and its grade does not transfer to jungle.

entries.why: Riplash into Shock Therapy or Skewer creates a dangerous pick when allies are in range to follow.
entries.watch: The grade depends on landing Riplash. Keep an exit and a second peel tool after a miss, and stay near allies who can convert the pull.

entries.why: Riplash into Shock Therapy or Skewer creates a dangerous pick when allies are in range to follow.
entries.watch: The grade depends on landing the hook. His 1.17.2 offlane results sit near the role average with no kit change, which does not justify a raise; keep an exit and preserve peel after a miss.

entries.why: A committed, resource-sensitive entry plus the weak dated Gold+ jungle reference makes this a practiced specialist choice. The stronger offlane reference does not transfer to jungle.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 lengthened Ashen Vow and Minueta cooldowns and cut Minueta's critical modifier, and her jungle results stay well below the role average over a larger sample. Offlane is her role; manage energy and avoid relying on the disputed Ashen Vow base value.

entries.why: Minueta and First Intent support repeated ability pressure; Swan Song can convert a reachable target while the team follows.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 lengthened Ashen Vow and Minueta cooldowns and cut Minueta's critical modifier, yet her offlane results remain above the role average, which supports a serious alternative. Energy, exit execution and the unresolved Ashen Vow base field make this a more demanding default than Greystone.

entries.why: Heaven's Fury and Heresy reward attack uptime after a catch; Crushing Descent gives Ascend a brief stun to open the entry.
entries.watch: 1.17 cut her on-hit and Heresy burn scaling and the Wind-Rider attack speed her plan uses, and her 1.17.2 jungle results sit just under the role average. Enter after key enemy control is spent; a visage reset must be earned.

entries.why: Heaven's Fury and Heresy reward attack uptime after a catch; Ascend helps choose the entry and preserve a route through the fight.
entries.watch: The dated jungle result does not transfer to her small, weak offlane sample, and 1.17 trimmed the attack-uptime damage both roles use. Enter after key enemy control is spent rather than leading into every interrupt.

entries.why: Siphon deals more damage to monsters and steals health from heroes, and Reaper of Souls stacks correctly after a 1.17.2 fix; Subjugate holds a target for allies as durability develops.
entries.watch: B after the 27 Oct recheck: stronger Siphon clears, a longer Colossal Blow and the passive fix lifted him above his 1.17 jungle results, but over a larger 1.17.2 sample he sits just under the role average. Colossal Blow knocks heroes back, so aim it so the target is not pushed away from allied damage.

entries.why: Siphon and Reaper of Souls support a scaling frontline; Subjugate can hold a target for allies as durability develops.
entries.watch: C after the 28 Oct recheck: 1.17.2 lengthened Colossal Blow and fixed his passive stacking, but over a much larger 1.17.2 sample his offlane results have not moved off his weak 1.17 level and sit clearly below the role average. Souls need ability kills, and Colossal Blow must not eject the target from allied damage.

entries.why: Line Tempo and Circle Rhythm support repeated trades before All-Kill! converts accumulated pressure; Rushing Beat helps choose the exit.
entries.watch: Offlane is the more established option. 1.17.2 trimmed All-Kill! damage and her jungle results fell back below even over a modest sample; she is a damage threat rather than the default damage sponge.

entries.why: Line Tempo and Circle Rhythm support repeated trades before All-Kill! converts accumulated pressure; Rushing Beat helps choose the exit.
entries.watch: Offlane is the more established option, and her offlane results stay near the role average after 1.17.2 trimmed All-Kill! damage. She is a damage threat rather than the default damage sponge.

entries.why: Air Assault can change the firing angle while Hypercharge provides a committed damage window.
entries.watch: Her carry results sit below even on 1.17.2 and below the leading options. Flight is not guaranteed safety; choose a peel partner, and remember the Satariel plan loses its takedown stacks on death.

entries.why: Relentless and Heightened Senses reward safe repeated attacks; Inner Fire turns an allied control window into a sustained barrage.
entries.watch: This priority assumes someone buys attack time. There is no dash to rescue an exposed path, and the initial control will not last for the entire barrage.

entries.why: Cybernetic Shell and Shield Bash let him hold the wave, then Shield Slam and Force Shield make him a team-catch and projectile-protection pick rather than a solo-lane threat.
entries.watch: Support is his established role; offlane Steel brings utility more than lane pressure. On 1.17 Heavy Metal attacks do not remove spell shields.

entries.why: Shield Bash and Shield Slam provide clear catch conversion, while Force Shield can protect an approach or the backline.
entries.watch: A on 1.17.2: with no kit change his support results fell below his 1.17 rate over a large sample. Heavy Metal basic attacks do not break spell shields, so keep a separate answer; catch value depends on allied damage close enough to convert Shield Slam.

entries.why: Shield Bash and Shield Slam provide clear catch conversion, while Force Shield can protect an approach or the backline.
entries.watch: Jungle rests on a much smaller sample than support; his 1.17.2 jungle sample is small and its interval still includes his 1.16.4 review rate, so A stays; it drops to B if a larger sample's interval excludes 52.6%. Heavy Metal attacks no longer break spell shields, so bring a real answer before engaging.

entries.why: Ruthless Assault and Highland Hurl can pressure a held target; Unstoppable Force helps a committed frontline sequence.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 strengthened Highland Hurl, but her jungle sample is small and below even, so this is not a default recommendation. Use her as a practiced control answer.

entries.why: Highland Hurl now slows or roots for 1.25s at every rank and shreds more armor, setting up Ruthless Assault on a held target; Unstoppable Force helps a committed frontline sequence.
entries.watch: C after the 28 Oct recheck: the 1.17.2 Highland Hurl buff first came with offlane results near even, but over a larger 1.17.2 sample she is back at her weak 1.17 level, clearly below the role average. Her damage scales with armor, so pick her only as a practiced frontline answer.

entries.why: Harvest Nettles supports repeated lane pressure; Fly Trap and Bramble Patch turn constrained movement into a clear follow-up opportunity.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 cut Harvest Nettles damage and Bramble Patch's ally speed, and her midlane results sit near the role average, so the S is flagged for recheck. The delayed ultimate still needs setup or a constrained path.

entries.why: Harvest Nettles supports repeated lane pressure; Fly Trap and Bramble Patch turn constrained movement into a clear follow-up opportunity.
entries.watch: B on 1.17.2: Harvest Nettles and Bramble Patch were trimmed and her support results fell well below even over a small sample. Support needs frontline elsewhere, and the delayed ultimate still needs setup or a constrained path.

entries.why: Vaporize now applies on-hit effects at higher effectiveness and Vortex Grenade scales better, rewarding ability-attack weaving; Rocket Dash lets him preserve a firing position or follow a confirmed catch.
entries.watch: A on 1.17.2: the Vaporize and Vortex Grenade buffs carry the move, since his carry results rose only to about even. Do not spend the dash forward while a diver is missing or channel Ventilate into an available interrupt.

entries.why: Peekaboo! marks a target for repeated Knock, Knock! shots with attacks between casts; Back It Up! returns a target to where the team can follow.
entries.watch: Carry has the better role result. The midlane plan stays physical with Sniper's Bounty, so missed shots cost both damage and gold; 1.17 trimmed Demonic Bargain and Satariel, which this plan uses.

entries.why: Arterial Grip grounds and slows a bound target so Rupture and Bloodbound can land, and Exsanguinate's bats return health, far more when they hit heroes. The grounding bind also stops dashes such as Torn Space.
entries.watch: 1.17.2 cut Rupture, Exsanguinate and Lilith damage and lengthened Rupture's cooldown, though his midlane results sit above the role average, so treat him as a practiced pick. No dash: crowd control on Valmont, broken line of sight or distance breaks the bind, and Exsanguinate costs more mana each second it stays on.

entries.why: Peekaboo! marks a target so Knock, Knock! fires again sooner, with ranged attacks between casts; Back It Up! returns a target to where the team can follow.
entries.watch: Mystic Marksman makes Knock, Knock! magical while his attacks and the grenade's hit stay physical, so penetration must fit both. Missed shots sharply reduce this plan's value.

entries.why: Cyclebreaker/High Impact and stance mobility support repeated pressure; 84000 Hairs can create an additional threat after a favorable entry.
entries.watch: 1.17 traded some health and armor for attack speed and cleave, so do not treat his damage plan as sole frontline coverage. 1.17.2 lets 84000 Hairs keep its stacks out of combat, but his jungle sample is smaller than established staples; do not assume clones copy item on-hit effects.

entries.why: Windburn's extended attacks reward reliable attack time after a mid or support catch, and Backlash and Quelling Gale protect that window from projectiles. She still needs a separate initiator.
entries.watch: A Ground effect now interrupts Lash Kick, so keep another exit. Reflection timing and target access decide whether her projectile tools matter.

entries.why: Windburn and repeated attacks create sustained pressure, while Backlash and Quelling Gale offer tools against projectile-based threats.
entries.watch: The offlane sample is small in both patches. A Ground effect now interrupts Lash Kick; reflection timing and target access decide whether her projectile tools matter.
